business_model.assessment: Mightylicious sells packaged gluten-free/vegan cookies, flour blends and brownie mix through direct-to-consumer online, wholesale and retail channels [A27, A28]. Payers are consumers and retailers/wholesale customers, buying one-time per order; no subscription or contract revenue is documented. Revenue is $459,216 in FY2025, up about 32% from $347,602 in FY2024 [A18, B2]. Cost of goods sold exceeded revenue in both years (gross loss of $29,477 in FY2025 [A19] and $117,069 in FY2024 [B1]), so unit economics are not yet shown to be positive. The issuer says vertical integration should lower COGS [B7], but no cost, timeline or evidence is given. The Form C does not split revenue by channel or customer. The reviewed notes contain boilerplate that does not fit a cookie business (customers 'prepay for services at the time of booking') [B6], which lowers confidence in the care taken with the statements.

competition.assessment: The issuer names four competitors: Aliea's, Tate's Bake Shop, Dr. Schar and Udi's, and says it competes with many large and small companies, including well-known global competitors [A29]. Differentiation is limited to product attributes (gluten-free, vegan, kosher, Non-GMO, taste, Gen X/Millennial target) [A27]. The pack gives no market share, pricing, margin comparison or customer-switching evidence. Risk factors name shelf-space competition, retailers' negotiating power and better-resourced competitors [A29]. Two trademarks are registered, but no patent or other durable moat is documented. Competitive position is therefore asserted, not demonstrated.

demand_evidence.assessment: Documented demand is real but modest: reviewed revenue of $459,216 (FY2025) and $347,602 (FY2024) [A18]. The reviewed statements are not audited and sales are not tied to named contracts [A24]. Stronger traction statements ('$100K MoM run rate', '1800 doors in over 49 states', Kroger/Giant/HEB/HyVee, Amazon +355% YoY) appear only in an undated testing-the-waters email, with no basis or period [A32]. They are not reconciled to FY2025 revenue of $459,216, so they are issuer assertions only. The email also says the higher run rate 'accelerated our cash burn' [B8]. Retailer contracts, purchase orders, channel revenue and any 2026 interim financials are missing from the pack. Wakefern and Wegmans launches are described as pending or Q4 2026 plans, not completed events [A32].

economics_and_funding.assessment: Reviewed FY2025 figures (year ended 2025-12-31, about 9.5 months before the cutoff): net loss $896,217, operating cash outflow $960,595, cash $116,414 plus $1,397,792 in marketable securities at that date [A20, A25, A21]. Total liabilities were $5,354,602, mostly SAFEs carried at $5,007,597 [A22, A23], leaving a stockholders' deficit of $(3,507,862). The accountant's report includes a going-concern paragraph [A24]. The issuer states $654,000 in cash and equivalents at 2026-06-30 and about 5 months of runway; this is an unreviewed issuer figure whose relationship to the Dec 2025 cash and securities is unexplained [A26]. I do not compute a current runway from these mismatched figures. Disclosed debt totals $139,475 (EIDL $80,000 secured by all assets, Wayflyer $51,000, CEO loans $8,475) [A17, B5]. The offering raises $75,000 minimum and $1,000,000 maximum [A5], and the issuer calls the proceeds 'essential to our operations' [A26]. Even the maximum is small against the FY2025 cash burn, and the issuer plans further capital raises [A26]. Intermediary fees and the onboarding fee reduce net proceeds [A7].

execution_risks.assessment: Key risks: (1) continued losses, with COGS above revenue and a going-concern paragraph [A19, A24]; (2) dependence on a sole officer, with 2 employees and the CEO handling a wide range of administrative and operational functions [A30, B11]; (3) retail-expansion risks, with Wakefern/Wegmans launches pending and new retail growth needing working capital [A32]; (4) heavy reliance on third-party suppliers, co-packers and retailers, and exposure to commodity and tariff costs, per risk factors; (5) the proceeds plan differs between Form C and press release (vertical integration and executive hiring appear only in the press release) [B7]; (6) disclosure quality issues: boilerplate in the notes [B6], unreconciled traction claims [A32], a custodian-name mismatch [A35], and testing-the-waters materials that the issuer says 'may not have included proper disclaimers'. Availability is unverified: the platform page was not reachable, and the press release describing the campaign as live comes from the issuer [B13].

price_and_terms.assessment: The SAFE is sold at $1.00 per unit of purchase amount; the price is described as 'arbitrary', which is a disclosure rather than proof of mis-pricing [A4]. The operative reference is the $15,000,000 pre-money valuation cap [A9]. The cap sits against 1,000,000 outstanding shares, an implied cap price of $15 per share before SAFEs [B3]. The cap is about 32.7x FY2025 revenue (arithmetic only, with no comparables in the pack) [B12]. There is no discount in the cited terms. Existing SAFEs with principal of $5,096,791 also carry a $15,000,000 cap, and equal about 34% of the cap [A15, B4]. They convert on top of this offering because SAFEs are excluded from the denominator [A9]. K1 and K2 ($1,000,000 and $1,075,000) simply multiply the $1.00 SAFE unit price by share counts; the $1.00 is a purchase-amount unit, not a share price. These figures are not a valuation of the company and should not be read as such [B10]. K3 and K4 are withheld. Investor-side fees are not stated in the cited text. The Form C 'greater of' conversion wording differs from the SAFE form's Equity Financing Price definition [A9]. The SAFE form should govern.

security_path_to_proceeds.assessment: The security is a Crowd SAFE held through a custodian/nominee; investors hold a beneficial interest only [A35]. Routes to cash are separate questions. (a) Conversion: it happens only on an Equity Financing, defined as the next sale of Capital Stock for at least $1,000,000 gross cash; the SAFE sale itself is not a sale of Capital Stock, so this offering does not appear to trigger conversion [A9, B9]. The issuer discloses it may never conduct one and is under no obligation to convert otherwise [A13]. (b) Liquidity Event (IPO, direct listing, change of control) or Dissolution: a cash-out right exists, but it is junior to debt and creditor claims, on par with other SAFEs/preferred, and senior to common; payment is limited to available funds [A10]. The notes' description of dissolution priority differs [A10]. Existing SAFEs of $5,096,791 share this pari passu class [A15]. The EIDL loan has all-asset collateral [A17]. No waterfall beyond the SAFE form language is stated. (c) Transfer: a one-year Reg CF restriction applies, plus opinion-of-counsel and no-competitor limits; a legal ability to transfer does not mean a buyer exists [A12]. (d) No voting, information or anti-dilution rights [A11]. The CEO ('Lead') controls amendments and acts as proxy [A35]. No public market exists or is contemplated.

issues.explanation: The A-stage input flags the existing SAFEs as 'conversion_terms_disclosed: true', but only the $15M cap is cited. The reviewed note says that for existing Crowd SAFEs the company 'may elect either to continue the instrument without conversion' on an Equity Financing (C4). This differs from the automatic conversion in this Offering's form. Discount, MFN and the actual existing-SAFE form are not in the pack. The flag should read partial. The existing SAFEs' share count cannot be derived from the pack.

Three documents describe priority differently: the SAFE form (junior to debt, on par with other SAFEs and preferred, senior to common), the Form C risk factor (payment only after creditors and more senior holders including preferred are paid in full), and the reviewed note (equal priority with common equity on dissolution) (C5). B recorded only the note conflict. The SAFE form is the operative text, but the conflict should be weighed. No waterfall or intercreditor terms are stated for the all-asset EIDL lien.

B5 says the amounts 'differ by date and Wayflyer status'. The pack shows more than that. The note table shows a Wayflyer balance of $31,795 at 2025-12-31 with maturity 02/28/2026. The Form C shows $51,000 outstanding with maturity February 28, 2027, and describes '1% per month' with 'Monthly payment of $1,989 per week'. The balance has risen and the maturity has moved. The note says no subsequent events needed disclosure through issuance (report dated 2026-07-23). Either a new advance or a modification happened and is undisclosed, or the Form C figure is wrong. Terms are internally inconsistent (monthly vs weekly). Request an explanation. This is not proof of misstatement.

B notes the cap is 32.7x FY2025 revenue (B12) but does not mention that the existing 2022 SAFEs carry the same $15,000,000 cap (C3). The cap therefore has not moved since 2022, while FY2024 and FY2025 revenue were $347,602 and $459,216. Investors from 2022 and this Offering share the cap but not necessarily other terms. This is a fact, not a verdict on price. No comparables are in the pack.

B6 found service-booking boilerplate in the receivables note. The Business section shows more of the same: 'institution integrations', 'institutional deployment' and 'white-label customer integration' (C6), plus risk factors on 'product candidates' (A28). These fit another business model. The 'lower confidence in care' reading is an analyst inference. It should be stated as such, with a request for corrected disclosure. It is not proof of misstatement. Execution risk item (4), which cites suppliers, co-packers and tariffs, has no claim ids. The risk-factor text is on p.17-19 and should be tied to claims.

B7 notes that the press release names vertical integration as 'a core use of proceeds' and that the Form C table lacks it. The Form C also says the issuer 'does not intend to make any material capital expenditures in the near future' (C7). Completing vertical integration would normally involve spend, and none is quantified. The two statements conflict, and the plan, cost and timing are undisclosed.
issues.target: B7 use of proceeds: vertical integration

issues.explanation: Critical item status is overstated. The pack's own checklist marks fees as missing, and A7 admits investor-side fees are not stated. Investors must open a custody account (C8). The custodial agreement's fee schedule is blank, says the Client pays fees, and sets payment terms. The SAFE says the Custody Account Agreement takes precedence over the SAFE where they conflict. The investor's cost of holding is therefore unknown. Also, the custodian name differs between documents (A35). Downgrade to partial.

B13 notes the press release (2026-09-24) precedes the Form C signature (2026-09-28). The same release says the campaign is 'now live' yet carries a disclaimer that 'No offer to buy or sell securities is being made' (C9). These are internally inconsistent. The Form C also warns some testing-the-waters communications 'may not have included proper disclaimers'. I do not find a violation; that is a legal question. It lowers the weight of the 'live' claim. Availability stays unverified.

The going-concern note counts only 'liquid assets in cash of $116,414'. The balance sheet also shows $1,397,792 in marketable securities, mostly municipal bonds (C10). B cites both but does not point out this tension in the reviewed note. The 2025 cash flow was funded in part by drawing down the portfolio. The $654,000 at 2026-06-30 is unreviewed. Its relation to the portfolio is unexplained. Read literally, the issuer's own '5 months' from 2026-06-30 ends before the 2026-12-18 deadline (C11). That is a reading of a stale issuer statement, not a computed current runway. No interim statements are provided.

Cost of goods sold per the note includes shipping, freight-out, fulfillment (Amazon, Shopify, Walmart) and warehousing (C12). The gross loss is therefore not a pure production margin. 'Unit economics not yet shown to be positive' is fair, but the gross loss cannot be tied to production cost. Vertical integration may not address fulfillment cost. Channel and SKU margins are missing.

A34 says the issuer may extend the deadline or raise the maximum, but the cited p.2 passage supports only the no-sale and refund rule. Extension and increase rights are on p.23. Partial support. Also, A13 'under no obligation to convert except on a qualified financing' relies on p.24 (cited in B9), not p.25.

A35 covers CEO control of amendments. It omits that disputes go to binding AAA arbitration seated within 15 miles of Wood-Ridge, NJ (C14). Together with a Lead who is the issuer's CEO and who both amends terms and votes as proxy, investor remedies are narrow. Enforceability and practical effect are legal questions beyond the pack.

critique_responses.response: B4의 34%는 달러 대비 캡 비율이지 지분율이 아니며, 발행사가 제시한 완전희석 지분(보통주 74.64%, 기존 SAFE 25.36%, 본 모집분 및 중개인 1.5% 제외)이 더 적절한 희석 지표입니다(C1). 산출 근거는 제시되지 않은 발행사 주장으로 표시했고 PC3에 반영했습니다.
'최대 모집액도 작다'는 표현은 과장입니다. 최대 $1,000,000은 FY2025 영업현금유출의 약 1.04배(C13)이며 수수료 차감 전 금액이고, 목표액 $75,000만 작습니다. 최대액 달성 여부도 불명입니다.
기존 SAFE의 conversion_terms_disclosed는 '부분'이 맞습니다. 캡만 확인되고 할인·MFN은 팩에 없으며, 주석(C4)은 지분 투자 시 전환하지 않고 유지할 수도 있다고 하여 본 SAFE와 다릅니다. 기존 SAFE의 주식수는 도출할 수 없어 PC2를 unknown으로 두었습니다.
청산 순위가 SAFE 양식, Form C 위험요소, 검토 주석 세 곳에서 다르게 기술됩니다(C5). 운영 문서는 SAFE 양식(부채 후순위, 기존 SAFE·우선주와 동순위, 보통주 우선)이며, EIDL 전자산 담보와의 관계는 문서에 없어 PC1 판단에 이 불확실성을 반영했습니다.
Wayflyer 데이터는 단순한 날짜 차이가 아닙니다. 주석상 2025-12-31 잔액 $31,795·만기 2026-02-28인데 Form C는 $51,000·만기 2027-02-28이며 '월 지급/주당 $1,989' 표현이 모순됩니다(C2). 신규 차입 또는 수정의 가능성을 질문 사항으로 두되 오류 확정은 아닙니다.
기존 2022년 SAFE도 동일한 $15M 캡이어서 캡이 2022년 이후 변하지 않았다는 사실(C3)을 추가합니다. 이는 사실일 뿐 가격 판단이 아니며 비교 자료가 없어 PC2는 unknown입니다.
주석 문구의 부적합성(B6, C6)을 '관리 소홀 가능성'이라는 분석적 추론으로 낮춰 표현하고, 정정 공시를 요청해야 할 사항으로 둡니다. 공급업체·관세 위험은 Form C 위험요소 17~19쪽 기반이며 별도 claim으로 연결되지 않은 점을 인정합니다. BT1에서 반대 근거로만 사용했습니다.
Form C는 '중대한 자본지출 계획 없음'이라 하면서 보도자료는 수직계열화를 핵심 자금 용도로 제시하여 충돌합니다(C7). 계획·비용·시기가 미공개이므로 사용처 불확실성으로만 기록하며 별도 평가 항목의 결정 근거로 쓰지 않았습니다.
수수료·최소투자 항목은 투자자 측 수수료가 미확정이므로 '부분'으로 하향합니다. 수탁계약의 수수료표는 공란이고 수탁계약이 SAFE보다 우선하며 수탁기관 명칭도 문서 간 불일치합니다(C8, A35). PC3의 근거에 반영했습니다.
보도자료의 '캠페인 진행 중'과 같은 문서의 '청약 권유 없음' 면책 문구가 충돌하고(C9), 독립 확인이 없어 모집 가능 여부는 미확인으로 유지합니다. 법 위반 여부는 판단하지 않으며, 예측에서도 발행사·플랫폼 자료로만 확인하도록 했습니다.

going-concern 주석은 현금 $116,414만 유동자산으로 보지만 대차대조표에는 시장성 증권 $1,397,792도 있고 2025년에 약 $758,853을 인출했습니다(C10). 2026-06-30 현금 $654,000은 미검토이며 증권과의 관계가 불명입니다. 현재 런웨이는 계산하지 않았고, 발행사 진술 자체가 5개월이라는 점(C11)만 BT4 fail의 보조 근거로 쓰고 핵심 근거는 going-concern 문단과 손실 수치로 했습니다.
매출원가에 배송·운송·풀필먼트·창고비가 포함되어 있어 총손실을 생산 마진으로 해석할 수 없습니다(C12). 'unit economics'라는 표현은 철회하고 채널·SKU별 마진이 없다고만 서술합니다.
A34는 인용이 p.2의 환불 규칙만 뒷받침하며 기한 연장·최대액 증액은 p.23에 있습니다. A13의 '의무 없음'도 p.24 문구를 근거로 합니다. 지원 확인 단계에서 부분 지지로 처리하고, 이 판단들에는 사용하지 않았습니다.
AAA 중재 조항(우드리지 NJ 15마일 이내)과 CEO가 단독으로 개정을 지시하는 구조를 PC3에 추가했습니다(C14). 집행 가능성과 실질 효과는 법률 문제라 팩 범위를 넘으며 단정하지 않았습니다.
본 SAFE 모집 자체는 전환 트리거가 아닌 것으로 보이나(B9) 이는 카운슬 확인이 필요한 해석입니다. 발행사는 인가 투자자 대상 별도 증권 발행도 가능하다고 했으며, 전환은 $1M 이상 지분 라운드에만 해당하고 시기·가능성은 팩에 없다고 PC1에 반영했습니다.
